title: Hajj – its rules and virtues
intro: The fifth pillar of Islam: who must go on Hajj, how its fard are done, and the reward of an accepted Hajj.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says: Complete the Hajj and ‘umrah for Allah. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:196)</small>

Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam. It is prescribed for every Muslim man and woman, once in a lifetime, if they meet its conditions. Hajj is the act of worship of visiting the Ka‘bah and the other holy places at the time Allah prescribed.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: Abu Hurayrah (RA) reported: “The Messenger of Allah (SAW) gave us a khutbah and said: ‘O people, Allah has prescribed Hajj for you, so perform it.’” (Bukhari)

items: The person is adult, and physically and mentally healthy.
The person has the means: money for the journey there and back, and enough for the family to live on until they return.
The journey is safe – the pilgrim will be safe in life and property.
For women there is one more condition – a mahram: a woman travels for Hajj and ‘umrah only with her husband or a close relative (father, grandfather, brother), or together with a group of women.

learn.text: How the fard of Hajj are done

items: Ihram at the Miqat. Near Makkah, at the Miqat, the pilgrims make the intention and put on the ihram. It is good to bathe and put on perfume first. For men the ihram is two white, unstitched cloths covering the lower and upper body; for women it is their usual modest dress with hijab. Then they pray two rak‘ahs and, reciting the talbiyah, continue towards Makkah.

Standing at Arafah on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, from sunrise. The pilgrims pray Dhuhr and Asr together at the time of Dhuhr, with one adhan and two iqamahs, and spend the time until sunset in worship and du‘a.
Muzdalifah. After sunset they go to Muzdalifah (between Arafah and Mina), pray Maghrib and Isha with one adhan and two iqamahs, and collect pebbles for the rami – the stoning of Shaytan at Mina.
Stoning at Mina. After Fajr on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah they go to the Great Jamrah and throw pebbles at it, saying takbir.

Tawaf – the third fard of Hajj. In Makkah the pilgrims walk seven times around the Ka‘bah, keeping it on their left, starting at the Black Stone (Al-Hajar al-Aswad) – turning their palms towards it if they cannot get close enough to kiss it. Then they pray two rak‘ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim and do the sa‘y (walking quickly) between Safa and Marwah.
After tawaf and sa‘y the pilgrims take off the ihram, and its prohibitions end. In the days of tashriq (when takbirs are said after the fard prayers) they also stone the other jamarat.
Before going home, they must do the farewell tawaf, and then leave Makkah. With this, Hajj is complete.

learn.html: From the moment they put on the ihram, the pilgrims are muhrim, and these things are forbidden for them:

items: marital relations;
indecent words and deeds, quarrelling and arguing;
hunting and killing insects;
perfume, cutting nails, shaving or cutting the hair of the head and body, trimming the beard;
using perfumed soap or shampoo when washing;
covering the head (for men), and covering the face (for men and women);
for men, wearing anything other than the ihram – no stitched clothes.

learn.html: Hajj is the crown of a believer’s worship, and the longing of every sincere Muslim heart to visit the holy places where the last Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (SAW), walked. A Hajj done well makes a believer stronger in faith and more faithful in following the Prophet (SAW). That is why Muslims should keep away from sins after Hajj, and try to keep the purity Allah gave them until they move to the akhirah.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “From one ‘umrah to the next is forgiveness for the sins between them, and an accepted Hajj has no reward except Jannah.” (Bukhari)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember – ‘umrah
learn.html: ‘Umrah is a pilgrimage to the Ka‘bah at any time outside the days of Hajj. Its rites are done only in the Haram, and they are: ihram, tawaf and sa‘y. With fewer crowds, ‘umrah is an unforgettable act of worship and a chance to visit all the holy places. It is especially valuable in Ramadan. The Prophet (SAW) said: “When Ramadan comes, perform ‘umrah, for ‘umrah in Ramadan is equal to Hajj (in reward).” (Bukhari)
